meta.description: Single source of truth for research ideas, hypotheses, findings, and failed attempts

ideas.title: BSiC₂ - Unexplored Ambient-Pressure Superconductor
ideas.summary: BSiC₂ predicted to superconduct at 74K at ambient pressure (Chen & Jeng, 2020). Zero synthesis attempts in 5 years.
ideas.failure_reason: Almost certainly thermodynamically unstable. No stability analysis in original paper. Phase separation to B₄C + SiC is thermodynamically favored. 5 years of silence = community consensus 'don't bother'.

ideas.title: Mg₂IrH₆ via Pressure-Quench
ideas.summary: Pressure-quench Mg₂IrH₆ (predicted Tc 103-160K) from high pressure to ambient.
ideas.failure_reason: Strobel's group at Carnegie already tried this in 2024 and failed at pressures up to 28 GPa. Mg₂IrH₅ remained more stable under all conditions tested.

ideas.title: Mg₂IrH₆ via Non-Equilibrium Kinetic Insertion
ideas.summary: Insert final hydrogen into Mg₂IrH₅ via kinetic (non-equilibrium) methods: cryogenic ion implantation, electrochemical gating, plasma-assisted insertion.
ideas.key_insight: Strobel's thermal equilibrium approach failed. Kinetic approaches haven't been tried. DFT shows no barrier for insertion - just need to get H atoms there faster than they recombine.
next_steps: Grow Mg₂IrH₅ thin films via PLD/sputtering
Cryogenic H⁺ implantation (<77K) to suppress diffusion

ideas.title: Nickelate Strain Engineering for Higher Tc
ideas.summary: La₃Ni₂O₇ superconducts at ambient pressure via substrate strain (SLAC, Feb 2025). Current Tc ~26K. Can systematic substrate/strain optimization push higher?

ideas.title: Public Repository of Failed Scientific Attempts
ideas.summary: Create a public, searchable database of failed synthesis attempts, negative experimental results, and falsified hypotheses. Science has massive publication bias toward positive results - negative results rarely get published, leading to wasted effort when others unknowingly repeat failed experiments.
ideas.key_insight: The absence of BSiC₂ synthesis attempts after 5 years reveals implicit knowledge that the compound is unstable - but this knowledge isn't documented anywhere. Strobel's failed Mg₂IrH₆ synthesis is buried in a paper about Mg₂IrH₅. There's no central 'we tried this and it didn't work' database.
ideas.problem_statement: When a theoretical prediction fails experimentally, there are three outcomes: (1) publish anyway (rare - no citations), (2) pivot to what worked (common), (3) abandon entirely (most common). Options 2 and 3 leave no public record. The next researcher wastes months rediscovering the same failure.
existing_attempts: Journal of Negative Results in Biomedicine (2002-2017, defunct)
PLOS ONE accepts negative results but they're buried
Figshare/Zenodo can host data but no curation or search
what_would_make_this_work: Low-friction submission (< 5 minutes to report a failure)
Structured format: What was tried, what happened, why it failed
ideas.mvp_approach: Start with materials science (most concrete). Partner with one major lab to pilot. Require failure reports as condition of using shared equipment.
next_steps: Interview researchers about barriers to reporting failures
Design minimal viable schema for failure reports

ideas.title: Minimal Complexity Threshold - Simplest Turing-Complete System
ideas.summary: What is the simplest system capable of universal computation? Rule 110 is Turing-complete, but is there something simpler? Finding the exact boundary between computational universality and non-universality would illuminate fundamental limits.
ideas.key_insight: We know Rule 110 works. We know simpler rules don't. The boundary must be somewhere specific. Finding it would tell us the 'minimum complexity cost' of computation.
why_interesting: Connects to Kolmogorov complexity and algorithmic information theory
Practical implications for minimal computing substrates
Would reveal what 'features' are necessary vs sufficient for universality
Might generalize beyond CA to other computational substrates
approaches: Systematic search through rule space with universality proofs/disproofs
Identify necessary conditions (void stability, bidirectional spreading, etc.)
Study bounded-time Turing completeness (weaker notion, might have simpler examples)
ideas.evaluator_notes: Deep theoretical question, computationally tractable, would illuminate fundamental limits of computation. Rated 8/10 overall.

ideas.title: Universal 'Interestingness' Metric for Complex Systems
ideas.summary: Find a metric that reliably distinguishes 'interesting' complex behavior (Class IV, edge of chaos) from mere randomness (Class III) and simple order (Class I/II). Entropy doesn't work. What does?
ideas.key_insight: We discovered entropy gaps don't distinguish Class III from Class IV - chaotic rules can have higher entropy gaps than complex ones. The 000→0 void stability is necessary but not sufficient. Something else is going on.
why_hard: May require multi-scale analysis (local vs global structure)
Might not exist as a simple metric
candidate_approaches: Logical depth (Bennett) - computational effort to produce pattern
Effective complexity (Gell-Mann) - length of shortest description of regularities
Statistical complexity (Crutchfield) - minimal hidden state for prediction
Integrated information (Tononi) - phi measure from consciousness research
ideas.connection_to_project: This is exactly what we've been hunting for in the CA/RD exploration. The Class IV isolation finding suggests the answer involves topology of parameter space, not just local properties.
ideas.evaluator_notes: Moonshot but transformative if solvable. Holy grail problem - probably impossible but if found would deserve Fields Medal. Rated 7/10 overall due to low feasibility.

ideas.title: Collective Intelligence Scaling Laws
ideas.summary: How does group intelligence scale with group size, communication structure, and diversity? Are there universal scaling laws? This has direct implications for organizations, democracy, and AI collectives.
ideas.key_insight: Sandy Pentland's work shows network structure matters more than individual ability for group performance. But we don't have systematic scaling laws like we do for metabolic rate vs body size in biology.
research_questions: Does group IQ scale sublinearly, linearly, or superlinearly with size?
What network topologies maximize collective intelligence?
How does cognitive diversity vs homogeneity affect performance by task type?
Are there phase transitions in collective behavior at critical sizes?
How do AI agents change the scaling laws when added to human groups?
data_sources: Prediction markets (Metaculus, Polymarket) - track accuracy vs participant count
Wikipedia edit histories - quality vs editor count
GitHub projects - success metrics vs team size/structure
Scientific collaborations - paper impact vs author count
recommended_contacts: Anita Woolley (Carnegie Mellon) - collective intelligence factor
ideas.evaluator_notes: Timely with AI, feasible with data, high practical impact for organizations. Rated 7/10 overall.

ideas.title: Precursor Availability Filter for Material Predictions
ideas.summary: AI systems predict thousands of new materials, but many are impossible to synthesize because precursors don't exist or synthesis pathways are unknown. Create a filter that rates predictions by 'can we actually make this?'
ideas.key_insight: BSiC₂ was predicted in 2020 with Tc=74K but has zero synthesis attempts. Why? Probably because there's no obvious precursor pathway. If we had rated this upfront, we'd have saved 5 years of implicit 'this is impossible' knowledge.
components: Precursor database: What compounds are commercially available or easily made?
Synthesis pathway inference: Given target, what steps could produce it?
Thermodynamic feasibility: Is each step favorable?
Equipment requirements: What does this synthesis need?
integration_targets: Materials Project - add synthesizability scores to predictions
Paper review - flag predictions without synthesis pathway
prior_art: Retrosynthesis in organic chemistry (but not for inorganics)
Some ML models predict stability but not synthesizability
ideas.evaluator_notes: Solves real problem in materials science, immediately useful, relatively straightforward. Rated 7/10 overall.

ideas.title: Null Result Futures Market
ideas.summary: Create a prediction market where people bet on whether hyped scientific findings will replicate. Financial incentives would accelerate detection of failures (like LK-99) and reward skepticism.
ideas.key_insight: Currently there's no financial incentive to investigate suspected frauds or failures. Prediction markets create one. The LK-99 room-temperature superconductor fiasco would have been called out faster if money was on the line.
mechanism: New hyped paper announced → market opens on 'will this replicate within 2 years?'
Skeptics can bet against, believers can bet for
Settlement based on replication attempts or meta-analyses
Winners get paid from losers (minus platform fee)
challenges: Defining 'replication' precisely (same result? same direction? p<0.05?)
Avoiding manipulation (bet against, then sabotage replication)
Regulatory issues with gambling on science
ideas.evaluator_notes: Novel incentive mechanism, could actually shift replication culture, prediction markets work. Rated 7/10 overall.

ideas.title: Human-AI Calibration Training
ideas.summary: Humans are systematically miscalibrated about when to trust AI - sometimes over-relying, sometimes under-relying. Create interactive training (like forecaster calibration training) to improve human-AI collaboration.
ideas.key_insight: Good forecasters learn calibration through feedback. AI users rarely get this feedback. A training system would show: 'You trusted AI here and it was wrong' / 'You overrode AI here and you were wrong' - building intuition for AI capabilities.
training_components: Present human with task + AI suggestion
Human decides: accept, modify, or reject AI
Track calibration over time (Brier score equivalent)
metrics: Discrimination (can human tell when AI is right vs wrong?)
Calibration (does human confidence match AI accuracy?)
ideas.evaluator_notes: Actually useful and underexplored. Proper calibration could prevent both over/under-reliance on AI. Rated 7/10 overall.

hypotheses.title: Pressure-quench can stabilize Mg₂IrH₆
hypotheses.test_description: Subject Mg₂IrH₅ to high pressure in H₂ atmosphere, then rapid quench
hypotheses.result: FAILED - Strobel group tried up to 28 GPa, Mg₂IrH₅ remained more stable

hypotheses.title: Class IV entropy gap = log₂(3)
hypotheses.test_description: Measure entropy gap between Class IV rules and their Hamming-1 neighbors
hypotheses.result: FALSIFIED - Actual gap ~0.95-1.3 bits depending on block size, not 1.585. Class IV rules rank 36th-52nd by gap, NOT highest.
hypotheses.lessons_learned: Verify striking numerical coincidences across parameter ranges. The log₂(3) match was spurious.

hypotheses.title: Void stability (000→0) is necessary for Class IV
hypotheses.test_description: Check if all Class IV rules have 000→0 transition
hypotheses.result: REFINED - Rules 110, 124 have 000→0. Rules 137, 193 have 000→1 BUT are color-complements. Criterion: stable void under SOME orientation. Necessary but NOT sufficient.

hypotheses.title: Class IV rules are topologically isolated
hypotheses.test_description: Check if any Class IV rule has a Hamming-1 neighbor that is also Class IV
hypotheses.result: CONFIRMED - 0/104 neighbors of canonical Class IV rules are Class IV. They are isolated local maxima.

findings.title: Class IV Rules Are Topologically Isolated
findings.summary: In the space of 256 elementary CA rules, canonical Class IV rules (110, 124, 137, 193) have ZERO Hamming-1 neighbors that are also Class IV.
findings.implications: Class IV behavior requires precise tuning - any single-bit change destroys it. 'Edge of chaos' is better described as 'peaks of complexity'.
findings.novelty_assessment: Web searches found no prior work on this specific topological property.

findings.title: Void Stability Principle
findings.summary: For a CA to exhibit Class IV behavior, the void must be stable under at least one orientation (original or color complement).
findings.caveats: Necessary but not sufficient. Rule 149 (Class III) has complement with stable void but is still chaotic.

failed_attempts.title: BSiC₂ Synthesis
failed_attempts.what_was_tried: Theoretical prediction only - no one attempted synthesis
failed_attempts.why_it_failed: Compound is almost certainly thermodynamically unstable. No convex hull analysis in original paper. Phase separation to B₄C + SiC is favored. 5 years of silence from experimentalists = implicit rejection.
failed_attempts.lesson_learned: Beware theoretical predictions without thermodynamic stability analysis. Zero experimental follow-up after 5 years is a strong negative signal.

failed_attempts.title: Thermal Equilibrium Synthesis of Mg₂IrH₆
failed_attempts.what_was_tried: High-pressure H₂ atmosphere up to 28 GPa at various temperatures
failed_attempts.why_it_failed: Mg₂IrH₅ remained thermodynamically more stable under all conditions tested. Thermal equilibrium approaches cannot overcome the thermodynamic preference for Mg₂IrH₅.
failed_attempts.lesson_learned: When thermodynamics is unfavorable, kinetic approaches may be the only path.

failed_attempts.title: Class IV Entropy Gap = log₂(3) Hypothesis
failed_attempts.what_was_tried: Claimed the entropy gap between Class IV rules and neighbors was exactly log₂(3) = 1.585 bits
failed_attempts.why_it_failed: Rigorous testing showed gap is ~0.95-1.3 bits depending on block size. The apparent 1.585 match was due to specific measurement parameters. Class IV rules aren't even the highest-gap rules.
failed_attempts.lesson_learned: Verify striking numerical coincidences across parameter ranges before claiming theoretical significance. Post-hoc rationalization (ternary state partitioning) was wrong.
